definition: Designing and refining the input text given to a model to steer its output toward a desired result.
details: Because LLMs are controlled through their input, the wording, structure and examples in a prompt matter enormously. Practices include clear instructions, role framing, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought and output formatting. The DAIR.AI Prompt Engineering Guide is a widely used practical reference for these techniques.

explainer.lead: Prompt engineering is designing and refining the input text given to a model to steer its output toward a desired result. It matters because LLMs are controlled through their input, so wording, structure and examples strongly shape behavior.

tiers.eli5: It is like giving directions to a driver: the clearer and better organized you are, the more likely you arrive where you wanted.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use clear instructions, role framing, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought and output formatting to shape responses. A pitfall is that wording changes can shift results, so prompts need testing.
tiers.paperLevel: Output is steered by the input prompt; common practices include explicit instructions, role framing, few-shot examples, chain-of-thought and specified output formats. There is no single guaranteed formulation.

explainer.example: A prompt gives the model a role, two worked examples, and a required output format so the response is structured consistently.
